NOTE
OS:  This operator is only supported under the  Microsoft Windows  operating system.
The Pangolin  CHOP  interfaces with Pangolin's  Beyond . Beyond is a professional laser and multimedia show control application. When Beyond is running, the Pangolin  CHOP  will send laser image frames to it. The image frames are created from either a  POP ,  CHOP  or  SOP .  See  Lasers  for an overview of lasers with TouchDesigner.
The Pangolin  CHOP  should work with any version of Beyond but it is recommended to use at least Beyond v5.1.
TouchDesigner Non-Commercial licenses will only work with the demo version of Beyond. A TouchDesigner Commercial, Educational, or Pro license is required to interface with licensed versions of Beyond.
Using a  SOP  Input : input points will be grouped by primitive, and point position as well as color attributes from either vertex, point, or primitives will be used to construct the points to send to Beyond.
Using a  CHOP  input : Input channels are determined by name:  x ,  y ,  z ,  r ,  g ,  b ,  id ,  zone . Only the  x , and  y  channels are required. Every sample will be interpreted as a point to be drawn. Points can be grouped together into different shapes using the  id  channel. If not used then all points will be considered as part of the same shape. The  zone  channel can be used to override the zone parameter value for each sample, adding the option to have more control over which sample/point goes to which zone in Beyond.
Using a  POP  input : similar to  SOP , input points will be grouped by primitive. A Point position attribute ( P ) is a required, and a Point color attribute ( Color ) can optionally be used. If  Color  is not specified then point color will be set to white. Additionally, a primitive  Zone  attribute can be used to control which primitive goes to which zone in Beyond.
See also:  Laser CHOP ,  Lasers .

Usage
Beyond must be open to use the Pangolin  CHOP .
The Pangolin  CHOP  will construct a laser image from the points of a  SOP  or samples of a  CHOP  and send it to Beyond. With Beyond open and the Pangolin  CHOP  active (with input) the laser image can immediately be seen in its respective zone in the zone viewer of Beyond. See below an example of sending a circle to zone 1 in Beyond from the Pangolin  CHOP .

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When disabled, the  CHOP  will no longer send to Beyond. The corresponding image in Beyond will also be cleared.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.name: source
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the source operator.

parameters.label: SOP
parameters.name: sop
parameters.description: Use a  SOP  as the source. Apart from position attributes, the  SOP 's point color attributes are used to determine the color output.

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Use a  CHOP  as the source. Input channels are determined by name:  x ,  y ,  z ,  r ,  g ,  b ,  id . Only the  x , and  y  channels are required. Every sample will be interpreted as a point to be drawn. Points can be grouped together into a single shape using the  id  channel.

parameters.label: SOP
parameters.name: sop
parameters.description: Path  to the  SOP .

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Path  to the  CHOP . The input  CHOP  must have  x ,  y  channels for the point positions. In addition, it also supports  z ,  r ,  g ,  b , and  id  channels. The  id  channel is used for grouping points together as a single shape. By default when no  id  channel is present, each point is separate and unconnected.

parameters.label: POP
parameters.name: pop
parameters.description: Path  to the  POP .

parameters.label: Zone
parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: The index of the zone to send to in Beyond.

parameters.label: Rate Mode
parameters.name: ratemode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the mode for calculating the rate of the image in Beyond. Note: this is not the rate of the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Percent of Projector  Sample Rate
parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Rate will be calculated as a percent of the default projector sample rate. Specify the percent using the Percent parameter.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: Specify the sample rate.

parameters.label: Percent
parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Specify the sample rate as a percent of the projector default sample rate.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: Specify the sample rate of the image in Beyond

parameters.label: Vertex  Repeat
parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: How often to repeat each point in the image (not including blanked points).

parameters.label: Vector  Frame
parameters.name: vector
parameters.description: When enabled, the image will be sent to Beyond as a vector frame. A vector frame will have extra computation done in Beyond, such as the addition of blanking points. When disabled, the image will be sent as points to the DAC, with nothing extra added.

parameters.label: Resend Image
parameters.name: resend
parameters.description: Resend the image to Beyond.

parameters.label: Enable Laser Output
parameters.name: enableout
parameters.description: Enables laser output in Beyond. Has the same effect as hitting the "Enable Laser Output" button in Beyond.

parameters.label: Disable Laser Output
parameters.name: disableout
parameters.description: Disables laser output in Beyond. Has the same effect as hitting the "Disable Laser Output" button in Beyond.

parameters.label: Blackout
parameters.name: blackout
parameters.description: Sends a blackout command to Beyond. Has the effect as hitting the "Blackout" button in Beyond.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: The term "Frame" is a measurement of time used (1) in the  Timeline , (2) as a time
parameters.description: unit in CHOPs, and (3) as a time unit in movie files that are read into  TOPs  and written out from TOPs. The frame rate is the frames per second ( FPS ).

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
